learning_plan.execution_strategy_summary: Alright, future FAANG-level engineer! This isn't just a curriculum; it's your personalized launchpad. We're leveraging your existing Java familiarity and academic Django experience to fast-track you into a highly sought-after full-stack profile: Mobile (Android-Java) and Backend (Spring Boot). This roadmap is meticulously engineered to bridge the gap from academic concepts to production-ready skills, making you incredibly attractive for remote software engineering roles, specifically Mobile App Developer and DevOps Engineer, within a tight 3-month window. We'll build, we'll deploy, and we'll optimize for maximum hiring impact.

weekly_micro_goals: Week 1: You'll kick things off by deep-diving into Advanced Java OOP, tackling complex design patterns and concurrency. Concurrently, you'll begin your journey into Data Structures and Algorithms, focusing on foundational arrays and linked lists, and setting up your Capstone Project's basic Java structure.

Week 2: This week is about mastering Git and GitHub. We’ll move beyond basic commits to advanced branching, merging, and collaborative workflows. You'll continue with more complex DS&A problems (stacks, queues, basic trees) and start designing your Capstone's database schema, applying advanced Java concepts to your initial project modules.

Week 3: You'll dive into Relational Databases and Advanced SQL, truly understanding schema design and powerful queries beyond what an ORM typically abstracts. Your DS&A practice will intensify with more tree-based problems. For your Capstone, you'll start writing core Java business logic and establish a local MySQL database connection.

Week 4: We'll wrap up the initial database concepts with indexing and optimization. You'll dedicate significant time to DS&A, specifically focusing on graph traversals (BFS/DFS) and hash tables. This week also includes a crucial review of all advanced Java and Git topics, ensuring your Capstone's foundation is rock solid for the backend development ahead.
technical_skills_to_master: Advanced Java (OOP, Design Patterns, Concurrency, Streams)
Core Data Structures & Algorithms (Arrays, Linked Lists, Stacks, Queues, Trees, Graphs, Hash Tables)
Relational Database Design & Advanced SQL (Normalization, Joins, Subqueries, CTEs, Indexing)
interview_prep_goals: Solve 20+ LeetCode problems (Easy/Medium) covering arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, and basic trees.
Articulate time and space complexity for common algorithms.
Practice whiteboarding basic OOP design problems.
what_you_will_build: For your Capstone Project (an iterative E-commerce/Social app): You'll establish the foundational Java project structure, implement core utility modules with advanced OOP principles, design a robust relational database schema, and set up a local MySQL instance. You'll create initial data models and services in pure Java, ready for Spring Boot integration next month.
job_hunt_action_items: Optimize your LinkedIn profile with a clear headline and 'open to work' status.
Start researching companies and roles that align with your Mobile/DevOps goals.
Create an initial resume draft, focusing on academic projects and highlighting Java and Django experience.
monthly_plan.milestone_deliverable: A fully functional Java application foundation for your Capstone, with a designed and populated MySQL database, all managed professionally on GitHub, alongside initial DS&A mastery.

weekly_micro_goals: Week 5: Time to unleash Spring Boot! You'll set up your first Spring Boot project, grasp IoC and DI, and start building RESTful APIs using Spring Data JPA. Your Capstone project's backend will begin to take shape with basic CRUD endpoints.

Week 6: Focus shifts to securing your backend. You'll implement authentication and authorization using Spring Security (JWT), handle validations, and integrate logging. Concurrently, you'll dive into Android App Development, mastering Android Studio and building your first basic UI layouts with XML for your Capstone's mobile frontend.

Week 7: You'll refine your Spring Boot APIs with advanced error handling, unit, and integration testing using JUnit and Mockito. On the Android side, you'll tackle Activities, Fragments, and their lifecycles, and start incorporating Material Design components into your Capstone's UI, consuming placeholder data.

Week 8: This week, you'll finalize your Spring Boot backend with API documentation (Swagger/OpenAPI) and ensure comprehensive test coverage. Simultaneously, you'll implement advanced Android UI elements like RecyclerViews for your Capstone, practice debugging, and make sure your Capstone's backend and basic Android UI are functioning independently and robustly. DS&A practice continues, focusing on Dynamic Programming basics.
technical_skills_to_master: Spring Boot (IoC, DI, REST APIs, Spring Data JPA, Security)
Android Fundamentals (Activities, Fragments, XML Layouts, Material Design, RecyclerView)
Unit & Integration Testing (JUnit, Mockito for Spring Boot)
Intermediate Data Structures & Algorithms (focus on Dynamic Programming, advanced graphs)
interview_prep_goals: Solve 20+ LeetCode problems (Medium) focusing on DP, advanced trees, and graph algorithms.
Explain core Spring Boot concepts (IoC, DI) and REST principles.
Design simple REST APIs on a whiteboard.
what_you_will_build: For your Capstone Project: You will build a complete, authenticated Spring Boot REST API for your e-commerce/social application, featuring multiple entities, CRUD operations, validation, and comprehensive tests. On the mobile front, you'll develop a multi-screen Android application with a rich Material Design UI, including navigation, RecyclerViews, and forms, ready to consume the backend API.
job_hunt_action_items: Tailor your resume with keywords from job descriptions for Mobile/Backend roles.
Practice answering behavioral questions using the STAR method.
Begin connecting with recruiters and engineers on LinkedIn, showing your progress on GitHub.

curated_resources.recommended_search_term: Spring Boot Official Documentation / Baeldung Spring Boot Tutorials
Android Developers Documentation / Philipp Lackner Android Tutorials
Java Brains Spring Security JWT Tutorial

monthly_plan.milestone_deliverable: A fully functional Spring Boot backend with authentication and API documentation, and a standalone Android application with a rich UI, both developed as part of your Capstone, ready for deep integration.

weekly_micro_goals: Week 9: This is where your full-stack vision comes alive! You'll integrate your Spring Boot API with your Android app using Retrofit, embracing MVVM architecture with ViewModel, LiveData, and Room for local data persistence. DS&A practice will shift to mock interviews and harder problems.

Week 10: You'll focus on professional development practices: comprehensive unit and UI testing (Espresso) for your Android app, performance profiling, and code review best practices. Begin your journey into DevOps by mastering Docker for containerizing your Spring Boot backend.

Week 11: Dive deep into CI/CD. You'll implement GitHub Actions pipelines for both your Spring Boot backend (build, test, containerize) and your Android frontend (build, test, APK generation). Start conceptualizing cloud deployment, perhaps deploying a Dockerized Spring Boot to a basic AWS EC2 instance.

Week 12: The final sprint! Polish your Capstone project by adding a professional README, live demo, and robust error handling. You'll dedicate significant time to mock technical and behavioral interviews, revise your entire DS&A knowledge, and aggressively apply for jobs, tailoring your applications with your polished portfolio.
technical_skills_to_master: Modern Android Architecture (MVVM, ViewModel, LiveData, Room, Navigation, Retrofit, Hilt/Dagger concepts)
Android Unit & UI Testing (JUnit, Mockito, Espresso)
CI/CD with GitHub Actions (for both backend & mobile)
Basic Cloud Deployment Concepts (AWS EC2/Elastic Beanstalk - conceptual)
Professional development practices (Code review, Agile fundamentals, technical documentation)
interview_prep_goals: Complete 10+ mock technical interviews (LeetCode Hard, System Design questions for junior roles).
Refine behavioral answers using the STAR method.
Practice explaining your Capstone project's architecture and design decisions.
what_you_will_build: Your Capstone Project will be a fully integrated, production-ready full-stack mobile application. The Android frontend will seamlessly consume the Spring Boot backend API. The backend will be containerized with Docker and deployed to a cloud platform (e.g., AWS EC2/Elastic Beanstalk). You will have CI/CD pipelines set up on GitHub Actions for both your backend and mobile app, showcasing automated testing, building, and deployment.
job_hunt_action_items: Apply to 5-10 targeted jobs daily, tailoring each application.
Actively participate in mock interviews with peers or mentors.
Continuously update your GitHub with polished code and professional READMEs for all projects.
Network aggressively, attend virtual tech talks, and engage with relevant communities.

curated_resources.recommended_search_term: Android Jetpack Compose MVVM Tutorial / Code with Chris Android
Docker Official Documentation / TechWorld with Nana Docker Tutorial
GitHub Actions Documentation / The Net Ninja GitHub Actions

monthly_plan.milestone_deliverable: A deployed, full-stack Capstone mobile application (Android + Spring Boot) with CI/CD, comprehensive testing, and a professional portfolio, all ready for recruiter review and interview discussions.

critical_guidelines: **The Ironclad 70/30 Rule:** For every hour of 'learning' (reading, tutorials), commit at least two hours to 'doing' (active coding, exercises, and critically, building your Capstone project). Your hands-on keyboard time is your most valuable asset. No exceptions!

**Time-Box Your Struggles:** When you hit a bug, embrace the struggle, but set a hard limit (e.g., 60-90 minutes). If you're stuck, step away, take a break, ask for help, or research. Getting stuck endlessly on one problem can derail your entire month.

**Build, Don't Just Consume:** Resist 'tutorial hell' at all costs. Your Capstone project starts NOW and is your primary vehicle for learning. Every new concept should immediately be applied, refactored into, or tested within your growing application. This is how you prove you can build, not just follow along.

**Ruthless Prioritization & Scoping:** Your 3 months are precious. Stick to the MVP for your Capstone. It's better to have a fully functional, well-tested, and deployed core application than a half-finished, overly ambitious one. Features like complex payment gateways or real-time chat can be 'stretch goals' *after* you land the job.

**Embrace the Imposter Syndrome, Then Ignore It:** You *will* feel overwhelmed. Every elite engineer does. This curriculum is intense because the industry demands it. When you feel inadequate, remember it's normal, take a deep breath, and trust the process. You're building a formidable skill set.
learning_plan.final_readiness_summary: Congratulations, future Software Engineer! By meticulously executing this roadmap, you won't just be 'familiar' with Java or 'know about' backend development. You'll be a demonstrable force. You'll walk into interviews not with academic projects, but with a fully deployed, tested, and CI/CD-integrated full-stack mobile application – a testament to your ability to build production-grade software from concept to deployment. Your strong Java background will be amplified with enterprise Spring Boot and modern Android architectures, coupled with essential DevOps skills. You'll be a candidate who can not only talk the talk but ship the code, making you an exceptionally competitive and versatile hire for any remote Mobile App Developer or Software Engineer role looking for a comprehensive skill set. Get ready to impress!
